_whyThePatternIsRepeated: The regex text is copied from limits.json on purpose, as the key. A pattern edited in limits.json without its probes updated fails the JavaScript test by name rather than quietly testing the old one.
_misses: Each miss is chosen to sit next to the boundary that decides it: a word character in front of `window`, an `s` after `Transaction`, `signInAnonymously` beside the Firebase names. A pattern loosened past its boundary trips its own misses first.
decoys: const stripes = drawStripes(ctx); const s = new Stripe(texture);
const ethereumColor = '#627eea'; // a planet named after the chain
_packages: `packages` holds script CDN URLs and the blocked package group each one serves, or null. Each CDN's own way of putting a prefix or a version around the npm name has a row, because that is where the two readers' hand-written path parsers could part. The nulls sit next to the boundary: a package that only starts like a blocked one, a blocked name on a host that is not a CDN, a scope with no package after it.
_bundles: `bundles` are whole games, small, each with the verdict both checkers must reach on it: `blocker` when anything refuses the upload, `warning` when something is put in front of a reviewer and nothing refuses, `pass` when gamePolicy has nothing to say. packages/preflight/tests/game-policy.test.ts runs each through platformPreflight and apps/pipeline/tests/test_game_policy.py through content.scan_content on contract 2027-03, so the jam scan and `opengame check` cannot disagree about one of them without a suite failing. Most are the review of 26 Oct 2026, by its fixture names, which found twenty shapes the preflight refused and the jam scan only mentioned.

#1068's review: an attribute value has its character references decoded before the browser fetches it, so . is a dot and this loads Stripe; both checkers matched the page as written. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for js.stripe.com.
The same with a hexadecimal reference, .. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for js.stripe.com.
The same with a named reference from the standard's table, .. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for js.stripe.com.

The URL parser removes tab and line breaks from anywhere in a URL, so a src split across two lines is one host. No reference at all; the page as written held two halves. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for js.stripe.com.
decodes to a tab, which the URL parser then drops. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for js.stripe.com.

The host parser percent-decodes, so %2E is a dot; an img src is not one of content.py's structured kinds, so neither checker followed it. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for www.google-analytics.com.

A fullwidth letter in a host is folded to ASCII by UTS 46. No reference; the page as written is not ASCII. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for js.stripe.com.
A percent-escaped fullwidth letter is decoded and then folded. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for www.google-analytics.com.
An unquoted attribute value decodes references too. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for www.google-analytics.com.

An event handler is an attribute, decoded before it runs, so " is a quote and the fetch is a request. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for api.stripe.com.

The code signature in an event handler, decoded: both browsers' getAttribute returned Stripe("pk_live_abc"), which is what runs. The handler fails for want of Stripe.js, so no request is expected; the signature is the rule.
A srcdoc is a page the frame parses again, so &#46; is . in it and then a dot. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for js.stripe.com.
A style attribute is CSS, so \2e is a dot once the attribute is decoded. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for www.google-analytics.com.
Guard: a decoded URL in an anchor's href is a link, a warning, as a link written plainly is; the heuristics read the page as written beside it. Neither browser asked for anything.

#1068's review: an SVG script's text is its text nodes joined, so the comment splitting the host is taken out before it runs. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for api.stripe.com.
#1068's review: an SVG script's text has its references decoded. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for api.stripe.com.
An SVG script's CDATA is part of its text, joined to the pieces around it. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for api.stripe.com.

An SVG style is markup, so its text has its references decoded before it is read as CSS. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for www.google-analytics.com.

An HTML style body has no references, but CSS has its own escapes, and \2e followed by a space is a dot. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for www.google-analytics.com.
The same in a stylesheet file, with \. as the escape. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for www.google-analytics.com.

U+3002, the ideographic full stop, is a dot to the host parser, in a script as anywhere else. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for api.stripe.com.

bundles.why: Mutation testing, 7 Nov 2026: a backslash written as a reference is a backslash once the attribute is decoded, and the URL parser reads https:\\ as https://. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for www.google-analytics.com.

Mutation testing, 7 Nov 2026: an .xml document is read as XML, its entities expanded, not only as text. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for api.stripe.com.

Second review of this change, 7 Nov 2026: of two declarations of one parameter entity the first binds, as for a general one, and both checkers had kept the last. Ran in headless Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, which asked for api.stripe.com; Chromium does not expand parameter entities.

Second review of this change, 7 Nov 2026: an xml-stylesheet instruction's href is fetched with its references decoded, and both checkers passed over processing instructions. Ran in headless Chromium and Firefox under the 2027-03 CSP, 7 Nov 2026, and both asked for www.google-analytics.com.
